data.title: How Useless Coin’s 10% crash puts the $0.13 demand zone at risk
data.description:
Useless Coin [USELESS] has taken a big hit as the general crypto records a week of bearish advances. The token prices have dropped by more than 10% over the last 24 hours at press time, amid negative on-chain sentiments.

The token is trading below its key EMA and on the verge of breaking below the demand zone at around $0.13.

With the token leveraged position shrinking and significant unmitigated liquidity clusters lying below the current trading price, could the current bearish run be prolonged? 

Useless Coin faces mounting selling pressure

Useless Coin has followed the bearish trend witnessed across the majority of altcoins as they reap from the recent unchanged FOMC rates this week.

The token has since recorded significant bearish advances to test the current demand zone that sits between $0.125 and $0.145 as negative on-chain sentiment reinforces concerns about demand.

At the time of writing, the token was trading below all its key Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) on the daily chart, leaving the short-term technical structure also tilted toward sellers. These EMAs could act as overhead resistance if the token attempts a recovery.

But with buyers having defended the zone on several occasions, this time it could follow the same trajectory. Notably, buyers have started to show up on short time frames.

Shrinking leveraged positions signals reduced volatility

On the derivatives, the token’s Open Interest has shrunk to just $32 million as of writing. This points to declining leveraged positions as traders and investors scale back their exposure as uncertainty increases.

At the same time, an unmitigated liquidity cluster worth $586K lies around 0.112. This highlights the price level as a key target for the network sellers before further bullish advances can be resumed.

In the past, similar zones acted as magnets to Useless’ price action. Moreover, the chances of the same repeating still remain high.

Can USELESS avoid further bearish push?

USELESS remains vulnerable while it trades below its key EMAs and tests the demand zone between $0.125 and $0.145. A successful defense could provide a base for recovery, particularly if broader market sentiment improves.

However, a decisive breakdown below $0.13 would strengthen the bearish outlook. Without renewed buying pressure, sellers could retain control and extend the decline.

As it stands, the $0.13 zone is the level to watch. Its ability to attract buyers could determine whether USELESS stabilizes or enters another phase of losses.

Final Summary

  • USELESS has dropped by more than 10% in the last 24 hours as negative on-chain sentiment and broader market weakness weigh on its price.
  • The network’s shrinking leveraged positions add to uncertainty as the token approaches the $0.13 demand zone, where a breakdown could expose it to further losses.

data.title: ‘Crypto moves forward regardless’ – Why Grayscale is looking past the U.S. midterms
data.description:
Grayscale’s Head of Research Zach Pandl believes that the cryptocurrency industry will continue to expand regardless of the outcome of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

In a report published on the 28th of October, Pandl argued that even if Democrats gain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, the broader outlook for digital assets is unlikely to change significantly.

Zach Pandl’s bullish crypto market prediction

Currently, Republicans hold majorities in both chambers. However, prediction markets suggest that Democrats could take control after the elections.

Such a political shift could influence the regulatory environment for cryptocurrencies, particularly as the industry has benefited from greater regulatory clarity recently.

Furthermore, the years under Joe Biden offer sufficient evidence of a challenging cryptocurrency market. Despite this uncertainty, Pandl believes three major factors will support the industry’s long-term growth.

Factors driving Pandl’s prediction

According to Pandl, cryptocurrency is no longer associated with a single political party.

Research from Pew Research and The Harris Poll suggests that similar proportions of Republicans and Democrats own or use digital assets. Furthermore, legislation such as the GENIUS Act received bipartisan support in Congress, demonstrating that lawmakers from both parties recognize the importance of regulating and developing the sector.

He also highlighted the growing U.S. national debt as a long-term driver of cryptocurrency adoption. This is what Pandl believes would encourage investors to explore alternative stores of value, including Bitcoin [BTC] and other digital assets, as part of their broader investment strategies.

Main players in the U.S. crypto market

That said, Pandl also argued that the cryptocurrency industry does not depend exclusively on the United States. According to Grayscale’s estimates, only 15-20% of global crypto activity takes place in the U.S., while the remaining 80-85% happens internationally.

Hence, Pandl put it best when he said,

Regardless of the outcome of the US midterms, users around the world will continue to seek out alternatives to fiat currencies as well as more effective payment systems, and foreign regulators will continue to put in place rules to support digital assets innovation in their jurisdictions.

Crypto market dynamics paint a confusing picture

Well, the current crypto market dynamics also suggest the same, as the global cryptocurrency market capitalization stood at $2.71 trillion at press time, representing a 1.6% increase over the last 24 hours. Meanwhile, Bitcoin‘s market dominance stood at 60.30% at the time of reporting.

Additionally, the 24-hour trading volume reached $162.455 billion, up 120.9%. However, the market sentiment remains cautious as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index has dropped to 30, indicating ‘fear,’ compared with 51 (neutral) a day ago, 50 last week, and 71 (greed) last month.

This suggests that despite the increase in market capitalization, investors remain uncertain about near-term market conditions.

Lastly, AMBCrypto’s recent report also suggested that Bitcoin’s much-anticipated “Uptober” rally has disappointed investors, with BTC declining 4.2% month-to-date as of 25th October, against its historical average October return of 18.1%.

Still, all of these are mixed sentiments, which suggest that the market is still uncertain with no clear signs of what comes next.

Final Summary

  • At present, Republicans hold majorities in both chambers, but prediction markets suggest that Democrats could take control following the elections.
  • Only 15-20% of global crypto activity takes place in the U.S., while the remaining 80-85% happens internationally.

data.title: Can IMX bulls hold on after selling pressure fuels daily losses of 12%?
data.description:
As the market crashed on the back of Binance being hacked, most altcoins were left bleeding. Immutable was one of the most affected altcoins on the charts. In fact, IMX recorded a massive price drop on the charts. The altcoin not only lost the $0.12-support but also breached $0.11, dropping to a low of $0.106. 

Soon after, it slightly rebounded though. At the time of writing, Immutable was trading at around $0.11, down 12% on the daily charts.

At the same time, the altcoin’s volume jumped by 218%, hinting at strong selling pressure as traders reduced their exposure. The daily turnover further confirmed the selling pressure, with the same climbing to a three-week high of $5.06 million.

IMX plunges as sentiment flips risk-off

According to AMBCrypto, IMX’s fall was driven largely by weakness in the derivatives market. According to Coinalyze, Perpetual Sell Volume on Binance surged to 41 million, compared to 39 million in Buy Volume.

Perps bet buying fell deeper into the negative zone, falling to -6 million. This suggested that more positions were closed than open.

The same can be seen when examining the Futures flows. In fact, CoinGlass data revealed that Immutable’s Open Interest fell by 8.4%, dropping to $16.7 million.

This metric has not been this low since September. The drop was backed by higher volume as derivatives volume rose by 268% to $37 million.

A hike in volume and falling OI usually imply greater market activity as traders close positions to reduce risk exposure. Historically, risk-averse sentiment towards derivatives has led to short-term market shocks that often preceded price drops.

Spot market takes a different path

While derivatives traders panicked and risk sentiment flipped, spot investors increased their withdrawals. On 30th October, Immutable’s Spot Netflow dropped to -$0.4 million.

The rising withdrawals, especially following the Binance hack, suggested that most investors moved tokens off exchanges to either cold storage, private wallets, or other safer protocols.

However, this could mostly be interpreted as bullish for the altcoin as such withdrawals also reduced immediate selling pressure.

Lower supply helps in boosting scarcity and could help IMX recover from the recent slip on the price charts. 

Can IMX avoid slipping further?

With the market in panic mode, Immutable seemed to be under strong bearish pressure. A look at its momentum indicators seemed to confirm this view too.

For example, IMX’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) dropped to 26 into oversold territory. At the same time, the Relative Vigor Index (RVGI) formed a bearish crossover, falling deeper into the negative zone, further confirming the trend strength.

Taken together, these two indicators suggested that the momentum behind the downtrend is strong and that the trend is likely to continue. Therefore, if the sentiment persists after the Binance hack, IMX will revisit $0.10.

However, if the exchange outflows seen over the past day persist, they could help absorb some of the pressure. In doing so, the altcoin will close daily at $0.12, clearing the path for recovery.

Final summary

  • Immutable [IMX] fell by 12%, breached $0.12, falling to a low of $0.106 before rebounding slightly.
  • IMX’s fall was driven by intense selling pressure as derivatives sentiment turned risk off.

data.title: MARA stock slides 8% as Bitcoin retreats toward $76,500
data.description:
MARA Holdings shares fell 8.23% to $6.58 during the October 30 session, continuing the decline it’s been seeing in October. The Bitcoin miner’s stock fell as low as $6.44, its lowest level since 2023.

Bitcoin was also trading lower, near $76,714, as MARA’s recent price relationship with it strengthened.

October erases MARA’s September rebound

MARA approached $14 during September before seeing a sharp reversal. At the time of this writing, it had lost more than half its value from that peak.

A recent brief attempt to stay around the $7–$7.50 price area gave way to another decline on Friday. Shares opened at $6.81 and remained below that price at the time of this writing

The session was still underway, leaving the closing price unsettled.

The chart’s moving averages also slope downward above the stock. What this shows is that MARA is trading well below its recent average prices, and its earlier recovery attempts have not helped it to reverse the broader decline.

Bitcoin’s retreat provides context

The comparison chart placed Bitcoin near $76,714 and had reached $76,500 during the ongoing session.

Bitcoin’s decline followed a retreat from around $87,000 in September and early October. The latest selling took it below the $80,000–$82,000 area, where it traded recently.

MARA’s chart showed a 20-period correlation reading of positive 0.78 against BTCUSDT. That indicates a strong positive relationship between their closing-price levels over the selected daily window.

The reading helps to show their recent connection.

Their displayed daily percentage changes also cover different trading windows, since Bitcoin trades continuously and MARA follows stock-market hours.

What would stabilization look like?

Friday’s low of $6.44 would be the first nearby zone MARA should be looking at. If MARA can continue trading below that level, it would extend the decline into new lows. It is worth noting here that MARA share price has not been at the lows we are seeing since March 2023.

If it could push back past $7, then this would be pulling above levels it has been comfortable with lately. Some consolidation in the $7; $7.50 area for the next few days could bring some sense that this most recent slide is losing its steam.

Bitcoin’s nearby reference sits around $76,500, close to its 200-day average. A level to watch if selling does continue is around the 75k low range found in previous sessions.

Both charts still show limited recovery from their latest falls, leaving the next closing prices important to see whether buyers can establish firmer ground.

Final Summary

  • MARA traded at $6.58, down 8.23%, after reaching a fresh low since 2023.
  • Its recent closing-price correlation with Bitcoin was at 0.78 as BTC traded near $76,700.

data.title: ‘Our collateral resides off-exchange’ – Ethena downplays $8.8M Binance exposure
data.description:
Ethena, the protocol behind the synthetic, yield-generating stablecoin USDe, has downplayed exposure to the Binance hack. The team clarified that all their USDe backing resides offchain with its custodians, not on centralized exchanges. 

In fact, for the Binance scenario, the team claimed only $8.8 million in unrealized PnL (profit and loss) exposure to the platform. 

The total unrealized PNL exposure to Binance is ~$8.8M, far below the excess reserve fund of >$60m.

In a separate update following the FUD tied to the Binance exploit, Ethena added that independent attestors, Chainlink and Llama Risk, have verified its overcollateralized backing for USDe. 

Each of these independent 3rd parties mentioned above have confirmed USDe remains overcollateralised by more than $60m at >101.0%.

But before evaluating the claims, AMBCrypto explored why the community seemed worried about Ethena’s outsized exposure to the exploit. 

Ethena’s massive partnership with Binance

Ethena and Binance recently signed a partnership agreement for RWA (real-world assets) basis trade. This involves Binance’s bStocks, which promised an 11% yield and a great expansion into a $150T opportunity in the equity sector for USDe backing. 

The deal was signed last month, but the exposure seems relatively small. 

According to Ethena, RWA basis accounts for $51 million, or 1.2% of its $4.54 billion collateral for USDe. Beyond the RWA basis, Ethena also uses the crypto basis across Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] to hunt for yield. The crypto basis segment accounts for about 17% of the USDe backing ($628 million) and is spread across Binance, Deribit, Coinbase, Huobi, Bybit, OKX, and Hyperliquid. 

Collectively, this is about 18% USDe collateral exposure to crypto platforms for RWA and crypto basis. In fact, the largest share of the collateral is DeFi lending ($1.3 billion) across Aave and Morpho. But Aave was also affected and paused operations after the Binance hack. So, the contagion risk fears over Ethena’s exposure to the exploit were warranted. 

However, as the project mentioned, it has off-exchange settlements (OES) or custody arrangements with Coinbase, Copper, and Ceffu. So, the risk may be limited, as the project said. 

In fact, Mikhail Kedzel, Founder of Yumi Finance, confirmed that Binance offers such off-chain arrangements to top institutional players. 

For everyone asking why: it’s because Ethena doesn’t keep funds in Binance’s hot wallet. They keep it with their custodian, and Binance just ‘recognizes’ it as funds stored at the CEX. Stuff only really available to the big guys.

It’s like the ‘custodied collateral lending’ design being explored by Aave. 

That said, the Binance attacker stole and dumped 217 million ENA ($34 million) for ETH. This dragged ENA below $0.19 after a 16% drop. Whether Ethena’s clarification on the Binance hack is enough to stop the pullback remains unclear. 

Final Summary

  • Ethena clarified that it can cover the $8.8 million Binance exposure.
  • Binance attacker sold $33 million in ENA for ETH to avoid seizure and freezing.

data.title: How can PEPE traders take advantage of conflicting momentum signals?
data.description:
At the time of writing, PEPE was down 2.50% in the last 24 hours, its performance noticeably worse than other leading memecoins. For its part, Dogecoin [DOGE] was down by only 0.94%, while Shiba Inu [SHIB] gained by 1.13%.

And yet, the memecoin has rallied by 7.42% over the past week. In fact, Glassnode data also showed that the memecoin sector, as a whole, has shed 3.1% of its value over the past week, less than BTC’s 4.4% or ETH’s 5.9%.

Does PEPE have a longer-term bullish bias, and should swing traders and investors be looking to buy? Here’s what you need to know!

PEPE bulls battle for control of Value Area High

The 1-day chart revealed a bullish swing structure in place. The key levels to watch were $0.0000032 and $0.00000536. A daily session close above $0.00000536 would confirm a bullish trend continuation.

Within this swing move, the Fixed Range Volume Profile tool was used.

It plotted the Value Area Low and High at $0.00000377 and $0.00000491, meaning 70% of the trading volume since 11th September, when the impulse move began, has taken place within these two levels. This also makes them important horizontal levels to watch.

The A/D indicator fell to new lows following the heavy selling on 29th October. Meanwhile, the Awesome Oscillator stayed above the zero line.

These conflicting signals did not seem to subtract from the overall bullish price bias PEPE showed on the daily timeframe. However, ideally, buyers would want to see sustained demand to keep the uptrend going.

PEPE swing traders can maintain a bullish bias

Over the past week, PEPE has oscillated between $0.0000042 and $0.0000056, and at the time of writing, was at the mid-range level. The technical indicators were neutral, with a slight bearish leaning from the Awesome Oscillator.

Traders and long-term investors can stay bullish given the daily timeframe structure, but should be prepared for a price dip toward $0.0000044 or even $0.0000038. Especially if Bitcoin faces intense selling pressure.

Final Summary

  • PEPE has shed more value in the past 24 hours than some of the larger crypto memecoins.
  • Swing traders and investors can maintain a bullish bias as the price challenges the VAH once again.

data.title: BEAM’s price defies market trends with multi-month uptrend, but what should traders do?
data.description:
Gaming sector and ecosystem token Beam [BEAM] has rallied by 45.2% in the last 24 hours, with a 1,115% hike in daily trading volume. The $241.6 million market cap asset has been trending higher since July.

While the rest of the crypto sphere panicked and sold after news of the Binance heist broke, BEAM’s price surged across the board.

This relative strength was likely due to its existing bullish momentum. It was reported that the Beam Foundation had burned all the BEAM tokens in the possession of the Binance hacker.

984.249 million tokens worth around $3.37 million were burned using the Gnosis Safe Burn Signature, which also helped explain the short-term bullish outlook.

BEAM continues its multi-month uptrend

In June, BEAM broke above the downtrend’s lower high at $0.0016, flipping its structure bullishly. The latest bullish continuation came when the $0.00356-high, made on 23rd October, was breached on the 30th.

The breakout was on extraordinary volume and the gains continued at the time of writing. Relative to the rest of the market, the latest bullish impulse move was highly noticeable.

It is likely the altcoin may be overextended. The RSI on the daily chart was at 82, once again in overbought territory. This does not mean a pullback will immediately follow though. A stretch of ovebought RSI readings earlier in October came alongside a 16.54% move higher over ten days.

Traders’ call to action – Take profits and wait for a pullback

The 4-hour chart showed that there were two support zones of interest right now. The first was at $0.00445, which was respected over the past 24 hours as a demand zone and the altcoin went to challenge the $0.0054 local highs.

The other support zone to watch was the $0.0034 order block that initiated this move higher.

Swing traders can think about taking profits and waiting for a pullback, or moving their trailing stop loss order to just below $0.0034, as per their preferred strategy.

A pullback towards $0.0040 would likely provide a buying opportunity. However, without a clear sign of a short-term pullback, BEAM swing traders need to wait and not rush to look for a re-entry.

Final Summary

  • BEAM token has been on an uptrend on the daily timeframe since June.
  • Latest impulse move higher has not settled into a pullback yet, and swing traders can choose to wait for a revisit of key demand zones before buying.

data.title: RUNE up 15% after hackers use THORChain to launder stolen funds — What next?
data.description:
THORChain’s native token RUNE rallied by over 15% in the last 24 hours as the broader market lost $160 billion in capitalization. The decline followed Binance’s hack, which saw the centralized exchange (CEX) lose around $6.30 billion.

Hence, the question: Why is the token’s performance independent of the general market right now?

Is THORChain abetting laundering of funds from crypto hacks?

Hackers have regularly used THORChain to launder funds stolen from the crypto market.

For instance, funds from the Binance hack were commingled to a similar address that received $388 million from the Bitget incident after arriving via THORChain. This evidence might be a suggestion that the same actor is likely responsible.

The pattern has been evident from the swap volumes and fees on the chain, which have increased significantly. Fees hit a weekly high of $11K, confirming a spike in network activity.

Swap volumes showed that a total of $62.08 million went through the mainnet, while $94 million was processed through its bridges in other wallets.

As far as the hack is concerned, $8.94 million was converted to Bitcoin [BTC], and Ethereum [ETH] accounted for $6.17 million, while other tokens were swapped for $1.18 million.

As a result of a spike in network activity, the daily trading volume of RUNE surged by over 393%.

However, users are still worried that the chain could be abetting the laundering of funds. This, because other chains like Arbitrum One [ARB] froze the funds, but THORChain did not. In fact, immediately after the incident, THORChain posted,

Digital money needs digital freedom.

While they did not support the hack directly, the language used combined with the timing of the post raised many concerns. One user on X mocked the post, commenting,

Free to hack.

RUNE faces resistance at $0.70 despite strong buying

On the price charts, RUNE rose aggressively from $0.58 to $0.723, but it could not stay above $0.70 for long. The brief dip below $0.60 came immediately after the hack incident, but the altcoin reclaimed it as the floor.

The $0.70-level has been a resistance for the past month, but the strong buying pressure failed at this zone.

Moreover, the MACD bars turned green and grew bigger, asserting the buying pressure. The Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) reinforced capital inflows into the chain, rising from -0.04 to 0.31.

Therefore, RUNE will remain in a bearish structure on the 4-hour chart unless $0.70 is turned into support. Otherwise, the altcoin could continue bouncing between $0.60 and $0.70, but there is a chance it could break down.

Final Summary

  • RUNE surged by over 15% as hackers moved stolen funds via THORChain, leading to high network activity. 
  • RUNE bulls are facing resistance at $0.70 despite strong buying pressure, suggesting that the rally could be short-lived.

data.title: PYTH crypto sees $179M drop in secured value – Can prices recover?
data.description:
Pyth Network [PYTH] has recorded a massive decline over the past day, with the asset plummeting roughly 12% to a new local low at press time.

The reaction, expectedly, followed the Binance hack incident, which reportedly resulted in losses of roughly $6.3 billion. However, a closer look shows that the protocol has also recorded one of its weakest-performing months.

Perpetual market activity has further fueled the decline, as traders concentrate capital on shorting PYTH.

PYTH records a $179M capital outflow

The decline in PYTH was accompanied by a massive on-chain capital outflow, tracked through Total Value Secured (TVS).

TVS tracks the total value of assets managed by the protocol, including bridged and native tokens. The decline suggests that market participants are pulling back from active utility. Over the past day, TVS dropped from $3.164 billion to $2.985 billion, marking an outflow of $179 million in the past 24 hours as of writing .

More concerning is that Pyth Network’s earnings have also plummeted significantly over the past day, according to data from DeFiLlama. Earnings, which track gross profit after incentives, have fallen to roughly $1,310 at press time, the lowest level ever recorded on a monthly basis.

In fact, this represents a significant decline from September, when the protocol earned $434,640. When earnings drop to this level, it points to reduced protocol utility as users become more reluctant to engage with the platform.

Perpetual traders increase short positions

Sellers have dominated perpetual trading activity as they continue to expand their positions.

Funding Rate data for PYTH‘s perpetual market shows a significant concentration of short positions, with the rate falling to -0.0172 as of writing.

PYTH’s negative Funding Rate, now at an extreme level, shows that traders have positioned roughly $36.77 million in the perpetual market towards shorting the asset.

When broken down by trader category, the data shows that whales, traders who control large amounts of capital in the market, have been key participants influencing price dynamics.

The Whale-Retail Delta, which tracks the difference between whale and retail trading activity, rose to 0.301 over the past day as whale positioning in the asset continued to increase.

Spot traders accumulate despite the decline

Spot traders, despite the negative outlook, have been accumulating the asset.

According to CoinGlass, Spot Netflow tracks the inflow and outflow of capital on exchanges. When outflows exceed inflows, it suggests that more assets are being withdrawn from exchanges, potentially indicating accumulation.

Netflow currently stands at -$1.56 million, suggesting that following the decline, more capital has moved out of exchanges than into them. This outlook may stem from investors viewing the recent drop as a discount.

data.title: Ethereum wallet permission used in Binance attack, Blockaid says
data.description:
Security firm Blockaid says an attacker used Ethereum’s EIP-7702 wallet feature to connect a Binance account to code capable of draining its assets. Its findings offer a closer look at the transfers flagged during the exchange’s October 29 security incident.

Key to the analysis are the wallet permissions. According to Blockaid, after a total of 50 different variations were submitted in a single transaction by the attacker, one permission kicked in, and the dangerous code got a route to grab money out of the account.

How the permission took effect

Through EIP-7702, an Ethereum account can delegate the execution of functions to a smart contract. Permissions are granted to the smart contract code, which determines permitted operations.

Blockaid noted that the said account had delegated to another contract with functions to withdraw tokens and Ether, with a specific “operator” address being authorized to access these operations.

Basically, the arrangement gave that operator a way to collect assets from the affected wallet, and even new funds that arrive in the account are not safe.

Fifty variations, one accepted

Blockaid also followed up and explained that the attacker apparently lacked the wallet’s current account counter.

That counter, called a nonce, helps to determine whether an authorization can be accepted. An actively used wallet’s counter changes as transactions are processed.

According to Blockaid, the attacker submitted 50 signed authorizations covering consecutive counter values. One matched the account’s counter when the transaction was included on the blockchain.

The firm summarized the result:

Only 1 of 50 was a hit.

Binance’s investigation continues

In its security update on October 30, Binance says the estimate of the incident’s total impact is about $6.3 billion. It said about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.

The exchange’s initial investigation pointed to a potentially compromised engineer’s laptop that allowed unauthorized withdrawals. Binance has said it would cover losses.

Binance has promised a technical report after completing its investigation.

Final Summary

  • Blockaid says an EIP-7702 authorization connected a Binance wallet to asset-draining code.
  • It has not been mentioned how the attacker was able to get the required signatures.
